title: Compensatory and long-range changes in picosecond-nanosecond main-chain dynamics upon complex formation: 15N relaxation analysis of the free and bound states of the ubiquitin-like domain of human plexin-B1 and the small GTPase Rac1.
buffer: buffer components that mimic physiological conditions, including 4 mM DTT and 4 mM MgCl2, at pH 6.8 in 10% D2O/90% H2O
experiment: 15N R1, R2 and steady-state {1H}-15N NOE at 600 and 800 MHz (14.1 and 18.8 T), joint extended Lipari-Szabo model-free analysis (RotDif for global motion, Dynamics program for S2, tau_loc, Rex)
construct_or_mutation: Human plexin-B1 Rho GTPase binding domain (RBD; human protein residues 1742–1862 plus two N-terminal lysines; residues numbered from 1743 as residue 1) carrying the W90F (W1830F) monomerization mutation; uniform 15N labeling
other_conditions: 1.0 mM 15N-labeled protein; tumbling: tau_R = 8.6 ns (± 0.43), D///D⊥ = 1.26 (± 0.12), axially symmetric (Table 1); related structures: 2JPH (solution structure of the free RBD, used for diffusion tensor analysis and Fig. 2b); regime (authors): Rex terms reflect microsecond–millisecond conformational exchange; per-residue S2, tau_loc, Rex, S2f at 600 MHz and R1/R2/NOE at both fields are in Supplement Table S2(b) and Table S1(c), per-residue S2 also plotted in Fig. 2a (仅图示/supplement for per-residue values; not transcribed here); 99 of 113 amides fitted; 36 sites need extended model; at least 4 N-terminal and 10 C-terminal residues highly flexible; loops L1-L3 mobile (S2 <0.8); most rigid: turn 32–36, helix α2 (96–99), turn 100–104 except residue 104
residues_author: Rex: 82, 83, 92 (~2.5 to 5 Hz at 600 MHz); low S2: 50, 54, 62 flanking flexible region 57–60 in loop L2; D59 (especially large amplitude fluctuations, flanked by P58 and P60); 78–82 (below regular secondary structure); 15 (end of β1); 74 (start of β4); 104; rigid: 32–36, 96–99, 100–104; termini: N-terminal 4 residues, C-terminal 10 residues; Table 3 regions 9–14, 16–26, 32–48, 50–57, 61–68, 78–84, 85–92, 94–103, 105–112
timescale: tau_s = 1–4 ns (36 sites, extended model); Rex ~2.5 to 5 Hz at 600 MHz (residues 82–83 and 92); 16 residues required an exchange term (all but 3 were less than 1 Hz at 600 MHz); Table 3 free-protein region averages at 14.1 T (S2 / tau_loc ns / Rex s-1): 9–14 (0.92/0.00/0.20), 16–26 (0.41/1.27/0.00), 32–48 (0.96/0.30/0.08), 50–57 (0.83/1.40/0.00), 61–68 (0.88/0.50/0.08), 78–84 (0.75/2.55/1.68), 85–92 (0.58/0.61/0.35), 94–103 (0.96/0.00/0.20), 105–112 (0.94/0.00/0.32) [extended Lipari-Szabo model-free fit, region averages]
author_claim: Free plexin-B1 RBD has highly varied ps-ns dynamics along the chain, with mobile loops L1-L4 and termini and few microsecond–millisecond Rex terms; it is more dynamic than active Rac1.
anchor: Relaxation data could be fitted for 99 of 113 amides yielding order parameters (Fig. 2a).
locator: Results, Dynamics in the free plexin-B1 RBD domain, p. 5; Table 3 (free RBD columns); Table 1; per-residue values in Supplement Table S2(b) and Table S1(c) of supp_PMC2667145_NIHMS92109-supplement-suppl.pdf; conditions: Materials and Methods, Sample preparation and NMR spectroscopy
caveat_note: Methods: sample preparation (W90F mutation), NMR spectroscopy; the entry card lists 298.5 K and 600/800 MHz, matching 298 K and 14.1/18.8 T here, but the card gives no BMRB entry or sample composition, so sample identity rests on temperature and fields only. Construct is the W90F monomerization mutant with C-terminal residues beyond the structured region (RBD residues 1742–1862 plus two N-terminal lysines); the card describes a 122-residue protein. Methods text writes the mutation as both W90F/W1830F and the field as 18.1 T and 18.8 T. Residue one-letter types are given in the text only for D59, P58, P60; other residues are listed by number only. Region averages are printed in Table 3 and were copied unchanged.

title: Compensatory and long-range changes in picosecond-nanosecond main-chain dynamics upon complex formation: 15N relaxation analysis of the free and bound states of the ubiquitin-like domain of human plexin-B1 and the small GTPase Rac1.
buffer: buffer components that mimic physiological conditions, including 4 mM DTT and 4 mM MgCl2, at pH 6.8 in 10% D2O/90% H2O
experiment: 15N R1, R2 and steady-state {1H}-15N NOE at 600 and 800 MHz (14.1 and 18.8 T), joint extended Lipari-Szabo model-free analysis of 15N-labeled plexin-B1 RBD in complex with unlabeled Rac1.GMPPNP
ligand_or_partner: Rac1.GMPPNP (C178S, truncated at K184 Rac1 loaded with the GTP analogue GMPPNP; 15N-labeled RBD with unlabeled Rac1 at 1:1.2 ratio; Kd ~6 μM)
construct_or_mutation: Human plexin-B1 Rho GTPase binding domain (RBD; human protein residues 1742–1862 plus two N-terminal lysines; residues numbered from 1743 as residue 1) carrying the W90F (W1830F) monomerization mutation; uniform 15N labeling
other_conditions: 1.0 mM 15N-labeled RBD with unlabeled Rac1.GMPPNP (ratio 1:1.2); tumbling: complex tau_R = 24.05 ns (± 0.99), D///D⊥ = 1.32 (± 0.08) for bound RBD, axially symmetric (Table 1); related structures: 2JPH (free RBD structure); no structure of the complex determined; regime (authors): amide resonances in plexin are in slow exchange on the NMR timescale, if they are affected at all by binding; Rex indicates microsecond–millisecond conformational exchange; per-residue values in Supplement Table S2(b) and Table S1(d), plotted in Fig. 4a (仅图示/supplement for per-residue values; not transcribed here); highest Rex (4–8 Hz) at N-terminus of α1-helix and α2-helix; β1 and β5 Rex 3–4 Hz; essentially no Rex for residues 64–75; compensatory dynamics changes on binding
residues_author: tau_loc > 4 ns: 15–26 (first long loop), 105, 108, beyond 113; Rex-requiring regions: all except N-terminus, first long loop, 64–78, 87–94; highest Rex: N-terminus of α1, α2 (92–99); reduced S2 on binding: 77–84, 50–58 (50, 54, 57, 62), 68–73; increased fluctuations: 74, 85–87, 91, 93, 96, 100 (significant S2 changes), α2; Table 3 regions 9–14, 16–26, 32–48, 50–57, 61–68, 78–84, 85–92, 94–103, 105–112
timescale: tau_loc > 4 ns for several residues in residues 15–26 and sites 105, 108 and beyond 113; 54 residues required an exchange term (Rex 4–8 Hz in highest regions; 3–4 Hz in β1 and β5; >2 Hz in many regions); Table 3 bound-RBD region averages at 14.1 T (S2 / tau_loc ns / Rex s-1): 9–14 (0.95/0.97/3.73), 16–26 (0.37/3.86/0.18), 32–48 (0.97/1.02/2.79), 50–57 (0.90/0.34/1.79), 61–68 (0.96/1.05/2.54), 78–84 (0.91/0.35/2.13), 85–92 (0.50/1.88/0.88), 94–103 (0.91/2.25/4.43), 105–112 (0.94/3.37/3.05) [extended Lipari-Szabo model-free fit, region averages]
author_claim: On Rac1.GMPPNP binding, plexin RBD ps-ns dynamics change in a compensatory way: reduced S2 fluctuations at 77–84 and loop L2, but increased fluctuations and many new microsecond–millisecond Rex terms near the interface (α2, residues 74, 85–87).
anchor: Also in the free protein, 16 residues required an exchange term to adjust R2 during the fitting (all but 3 were less than 1 Hz at 600 MHz), whereas 54 residues required such a term for the bound state.
locator: Results, Main-chain fluctuations in the plexin-B1 RBD complexed with Rac1.GMPPNP, p. 7; Table 3 (bound RBD columns); Table 1; per-residue values in Supplement Table S2(b) and Table S1(d) of supp_PMC2667145_NIHMS92109-supplement-suppl.pdf; conditions: Materials and Methods, Sample preparation
caveat_note: Methods: sample preparation (W90F mutation), NMR spectroscopy; the entry card lists 298.5 K and 600/800 MHz, matching 298 K and 14.1/18.8 T here, but the card gives no BMRB entry or sample composition, so sample identity rests on temperature and fields only. Rac1-bound sample is not described by the card, so same-sample status is unclear. Complex correlation times disagree between text (average 24.5 ns, anisotropy 1.31) and Table 1 (24.05 ns/1.32 for bound RBD; 25.05 ns/1.30 for bound Rac1); both are reported as printed. Rac1 relaxation data (free and bound) are in the paper but belong to a different protein and were not turned into rows. The authors state the data cannot show how far changes in neighbouring regions are coupled, and LS analysis gives no state populations.
related_structures: 2JPH (solution NMR structure of the free plexin-B1 RBD); 1MH1 (Rac1.GMPPNP crystal structure, partner only)

title: Compensatory and long-range changes in picosecond-nanosecond main-chain dynamics upon complex formation: 15N relaxation analysis of the free and bound states of the ubiquitin-like domain of human plexin-B1 and the small GTPase Rac1.
buffer: buffer components that mimic physiological conditions, including 4 mM DTT and 4 mM MgCl2, at pH 6.8 in 10% D2O/90% H2O

ligand_or_partner: Rac1.GMPPNP (Kd ~6 μM; no binding detected for Rac1.GDP)
construct_or_mutation: Human plexin-B1 Rho GTPase binding domain (RBD; human protein residues 1742–1862 plus two N-terminal lysines; residues numbered from 1743 as residue 1) carrying the W90F (W1830F) monomerization mutation; uniform 15N labeling
other_conditions: regime (authors): amide resonances in plexin are in slow exchange on the NMR timescale, if they are affected at all by binding; 21 of 113 RBD amides significantly shifted; a small number of RBD resonances unassigned, most likely due to conformational exchange regionally at the RBD–Rac1.GMPPNP interface; related structures: 2JPH; spectra in Supplement Fig. S1 (仅图示 for per-residue shifts)
author_claim: Plexin RBD amides affected by Rac1.GMPPNP binding are in slow exchange; a few interface resonances remain unassigned, likely from conformational exchange.
anchor: Amide resonances in plexin are in slow exchange on the NMR timescale, if they are affected at all by binding
locator: Results, Assignments of resonances from the bound proteins, p. 3 and Supplement Fig. S1; conditions: Materials and Methods
